thread:
sam: Heads-up — hit a weird parity issue between Node SDK and REST for text generation. our E2E tests started flaking after we switched to SDK in the sample-app. REST stable outputs, SDK outputs vary. looks like temperature defaults differ? :thinking_face:

kyle: can you paste a repro?

sam: yep. REST call (no temperature set):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small-001","input":"Summarize: Redwood mission"}'
```
returns same summary each run (expected). Node SDK call used exactly same payload omitting temperature: 
```js
await client.generate({model:'rwd-small-001', input:'Summarize: Redwood mission'})
```
but SDK returns different summaries across runs.

jen: odd. server shouldn't change behavior based on client. does SDK send an explicit temperature value?

mara: adding a tcpdump confirmed that SDK sends "temperature":0.7 in the JSON body when omitted. REST call doesn't send temperature at all. server default is 0 and behaves deterministically.

mae: :grimacing: that's a huge cost/regression vector for deterministic tests and billing. where is 0.7 coming from?

kyle: likely a historical default in the client generator. older client libraries defaulted to 0.7, and new autogen got inconsistent defaults. I'll search the generator templates.

sam: the sample-app E2E specifically relied on deterministic summaries for snapshot tests, which is why they started failing.

jen: do we have an obvious mitigation? we could patch SDK to not include temperature when unset, or set server to prefer explicit null over client defaults. which is safer?

mae: server-side change is risky because it could break users who relied on explicit client defaults. better to align SDK with server semantics: omit optional fields if user didn't set them. Also add clear docs on client-side defaults.

kyle: agree. I'll open INF-3499 to track. quick fix: change generator templates so primitives are optional and not serialized when undefined. Long-term: add a test that compares curl vs SDK payload parity for a small matrix of fields.

devx-bot: Created issue INF-3499: "SDKs should not emit implicit default for optional generation params (temperature)" assigned to kyle.

kyle: PR 702 opened that 1) stops serializing undefined optional fields in Node SDK, 2) adds a regression test against localdev to ensure REST and SDK payloads match when caller omits fields.

sam: nice. any chance we can also ship a changelog warning? some users may have intentionally relied on old client defaults.

mara: yes add a breaking-change note: "SDKs: previously implicit temperature defaulted to 0.7; new behavior omits unset fields and respects server defaults." and include migration note how to explicitly set temperature if desired.

kyle: cutting 1.4.1-patch with the serialization fix. ETA ~45m. I'll coordinate with sample-app maintainers to pin the patched client.

j en: also let's add a small QA checklist: generate parity smoke test for sample-app CI, and a docs snippet showing curl vs SDK examples side-by-side. saves more tickets.

mae: agree, adding to devex onboarding checklist.

devx-bot: INF-3499 status -> in_progress, linked PR 702, release candidate 1.4.1-rc1.

kyle: released 1.4.1-patch. sample-app pinned and snapshot tests now stable. closing INF-3499 after 2 successful CI runs.

sam: verified locally and in CI. huge improvement. thanks all :raised_hands:

mara: great catch. can we add a lint rule in the generator to flag defaulted primitive fields so this doesn't regress?

kyle: on it, filing a follow-up INF-3505 for generator linting.

devx-bot: INF-3505 created for generator lint rule.
